title: Corporate Financial Planning & Analysis Professional (Cert FP&A): Preparation Course - Part 1
overview: In today’s competitive landscape, financial planning and analysis have become vital for organizational success. Financial professionals are increasingly expected to deliver accurate information and insightful analysis to support strategic decision-making. Top management relies on these professionals to provide confidence in budgets, forecasts, and projections.

This course offers an excellent opportunity to prepare for the Certified Corporate Financial Planning & Analysis Professional (FP&A) designation by the Association of Financial Professionals (AFP). The certification validates expertise in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis. This preparation course covers the key concepts from Part 1 of the exam and practical applications of building financial models in Excel, which are central to Part 2. Enhance your skills, ace the exam, and set yourself apart in the field.
audience: This course is ideal for accounting and finance professionals currently working or aspiring to work in financial planning, analysis, budgeting, and forecasting roles.
methodology: The course focuses on key exam topics and addresses challenging areas through hands-on exercises, workshops, and real-world scenarios to strengthen understanding and retention.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Identify and leverage sources of company and industry information, applying macroeconomic and strategic planning concepts.
Understand financial and microeconomic principles and recognize various budget types.
Perform financial and variance analysis, drawing meaningful insights.
Build financial projections, evaluate capital expenditures, and conduct "what-if" analyses.
Utilize advanced spreadsheet tools such as pivot tables, value lookups, and macros for financial modeling.

items.text: Sources of historical financial data and corporate structure
Understanding the company’s business environment: business models, financial ratios, and industry metrics
Reading and analyzing corporate annual reports
Identifying peer groups and competitors
Key macroeconomic concepts: consumer price index, GDP, exchange rates, interest rates, inflation, and more
Evaluating tax policy implications on projections
Risk management fundamentals:
Value at risk
Hedging and insurance
Interest rate risk
Diversification
Identifying and analyzing financial and non-financial KPIs
Strategic planning tools:
SWOT Analysis
Porter’s Five Forces
Growth Share Matrix
Information gathering techniques: templates, surveys, and stakeholder communication
Finance principles and corporate finance activities
Core financial concepts and formulas: time value, opportunity costs, debt structures, and cost of capital
Financial accounting principles and their interrelationship across financial statements
Microeconomic concepts: marginal costs, pricing, and elasticity
Managerial and cost accounting fundamentals:
Cost allocation
Contribution margins
Fixed vs. variable costs
Budgeting and forecasting methodologies: zero-based budgeting, rolling forecasts, and more
Financial close processes and FP&A’s role in reporting
Effective communication and presentation techniques: building alliances, preparing reports, and visualizing data with charts/graphs
Validating financial models through consistency checks and reasonableness assessments
Identifying and interpreting data outliers
Conducting variance analysis: actuals vs. plan, forecast, and prior periods
Applying financial ratio analysis: liquidity, debt/equity, and efficiency ratios
Competitive analysis through benchmarking and peer group evaluations
Identifying industry or business seasonality
Incorporating common statistical concepts in analysis
Developing income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow projections
Evaluating capital expenditures and investments:
Net present value (NPV) and internal rate of return (IRR)
Discounted cash flow analysis
Forecasting revenue, expenses, and staffing needs
Creating "what-if" scenarios and sensitivity analyses to assess risk
Advanced spreadsheet functions for financial modeling:
Pivot tables, value lookups, and macros
Financial and statistical calculations: standard deviation, regression, and correlation
Documenting and maintaining models:
Assumptions, protocols, and version control
Overview of financial software and systems:
Business intelligence tools
Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems
General ledger systems
